# Put it into Practice {.unnumbered}

Now it's time to try things out for yourself. Complete each of the following steps, based on what we learned in this chapter.

::: {.content-visible unless-profile="excel"}
Unless your instructor tells you otherwise, use an [do-file]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"}[R script]{.content-visible when-profile="r"} to execute all code needed to accomplish the following (note: step 1 can be completed outside of [Stata]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"}[R]{.content-visible when-profile="r"}):
:::

1.  Download the `ed_nonprofits.zip` file, which can be found [here](https://learndata.net/ed_nonprofits.zip) and save it on your computer. Extract the files (unzip it) in a convenient folder on your computer.

2.  [Set your working director to the folder where the unzipped files are located.]{.content-visible unless-profile="excel"} Import each file of the three files from the zip file into [Stata]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"}[R]{.content-visible when-profile="r"}, one at a time. Create a file where you can record notes (e.g., a Word file). For each file, write down the name of each file (including the file ending), and then indicate which variable appears first (as the first column) in each file.

3.  Generate summary statistics for quantitative variables for the following variables: `staff_boardmmbr_2024`, `finance_rev_indvdon_pct`, `staff_fulltime_2023`, `pplsrv_numserved`. You can use any of the three files, since all have equivalent data.

4.  Generate frequency tables for the following variables: `sizestrata`, `peer_group`.

::: {.content-visible unless-profile="excel"}
After completing all of this, you should save your [do-file]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"}[R script]{.content-visible when-profile="r"} in a folder that is convenient to access. If you are submitting work to an instructor, they will likely want you to send them both your [do-file]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"}[R script]{.content-visible when-profile="r"} and a Word doc containing your results for items 2, 3, and 4 above.
:::
